subject: Physics
topic: Light travels in straight lines (ray model)
title: Light Travels in Straight Lines
summary: You can hear a friend round a corner but not see them: sound bends, light travels in straight lines. We draw its path as a ray.

notes.title: 01 – Light Travels in Straight Lines (Ray Model)

keyPoints: In a uniform medium light travels in **straight lines**.
Sharp shadows and the 3-card test are the evidence.
Sound (wavelength ~1 m) bends round corners; light (< 0.001 mm) practically does not.

blocks.alt: A candle seen through holes in 3 cards only when they are aligned
blocks.caption: Aligned holes: the flame is seen. Move a card: blocked.

blocks.alt: Rays from a point source graze a ball and form a sharp shadow
blocks.caption: Edge rays stay straight, so the shadow is sharp.

blocks.p: The ray model works for everyday sizes because light's wavelength is tiny; it is a model, not the whole story.

options: a straight line with an arrow showing the path of light
quiz.explain: A ray shows the path and direction of light.

quiz.q: In the 3-card test the candle is seen only when:
options: the holes are in one straight line

quiz.q: Why do we hear but not see a person round a corner?
options: Sound bends round corners; light travels practically straight
quiz.explain: Sound's large wavelength lets it bend; light's tiny wavelength does not.
Many rays together make a beam.

simulation.reason: The evidence is a classroom activity (the 3-card test) shown in the video with a real photograph and in the notes; a simulation would only repeat it.
